full_judgment: 6. The appellate court on consideration of evidence on record and the legal aspect of the case has found that the kabuliyat, dated 25.1.66, Ext. 2, is hit by section 15-A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (herein after called the Act) and the said lease was null and void and as such the land stood forfeited to Government. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioners, has frankly admitted that the basic document of the plaintiffs' title, i.e. Ext. 2, is hit by the provisions of section 75-A. of the Act and on the basis of the said kabuliyat, Ext. 2 and the kabala, Ext. 1, the plaintiffs have not acquired any title to the suit land. But he contended that as the kabuliyat, Ext. 2, is null and void, the title to the suit land will remain unaffected with the lessors and the land can not be legally forfeited Mr. Hemayet Uddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 6 (opposite party No. 1) has argued that provisions of sub-section (2) of section 75-A of the Act indicate that forfeiture will operate at once and the Government will acquit light to the land as soon as sub-letting is made in contravention of sub-section (1) of the said section. Now the question that arises from the facts and circumstances of the case is; that to whom the suit land will go on the violation of sub-section (1) of section 75-A of the Act. i.e. whether title to the suit land would remain with leaser or it would vest with the Government.
